subject.title: fix(sqlite): stop mount probes blocking database startup

question: Should fallback mount classification move to an asynchronous pre-database-open boundary, or should OpenClaw remove the command fallback and conservatively use rollback journaling whenever native classification is unavailable?
rationale: The current synchronous API cannot provide the promised hard deadline, while removing or changing the fallback affects persistent journal mode and startup performance; repository evidence does not safely resolve that boundary choice.

options.title: Classify asynchronously before open
options.body: Prepare the filesystem classification with a genuinely bounded asynchronous child process before entering the synchronous SQLite-open path, preserving WAL for confirmed local storage.

options.title: Remove the command fallback
options.body: Treat unavailable native classification as unknown and select rollback journaling without launching an external process, accepting the local-storage performance tradeoff.

options.title: Accept the best-effort timeout
options.body: Land the synchronous timeout while explicitly accepting that an unexited child may still block startup and that slow probes may switch existing databases to rollback journaling.

recommendation.title: Classify asynchronously before open
recommendation.body: Prepare the filesystem classification with a genuinely bounded asynchronous child process before entering the synchronous SQLite-open path, preserving WAL for confirmed local storage.
